summary: Luke Badiali reviewed sales execution with Andrew Fenwick and Kate Rowley, starting from the bid/no-bid checklist and two recent proposals. Elmstead bids on too much and qualifies too little, and discovery is often skipped when a tender lands. We agreed a scored bid/no-bid gate and a discovery call standard for every pre-tender conversation.

discussion.keyPoints: Kate said the firm submitted 46 bids last year and won 10. The bid/no-bid checklist exists but is ignored when partners feel a bid is close to their expertise.
Luke reviewed two proposals and found neither named the buyer's regulatory deadline, which conflicts with the narrative agreed in week 2. Andrew agreed discovery is the weak link.
Each bid costs around 12 consultant days. Andrew raised concern that cutting bids will look like less ambition to the board.

recommendations.recommendation: Introduce a scored bid/no-bid gate out of 20 points; only bid above 14 unless the Managing Director overrides in writing.
Every pre-tender conversation to capture the buyer's regulatory deadline, budget holder and current supplier on a one-page discovery note.
Cut bid volume from 46 to around 25 a year and reinvest the saved consultant days into pre-tender shaping.
Run a monthly bid review clinic led by Kate, reviewing one live bid and one loss each time.
Build a response sheet for the 'you are too small for this' objection, citing the 40 consultant bench and associate network.

actions.action: Rewrite the bid/no-bid checklist into the 20-point scored gate
Brief the board on the plan to reduce bid volume

nextFocus: Design pipeline stages that reflect pre-tender shaping as well as formal bids.
nextPreparation: Kate to export all open opportunities with their current stage and value.

tests.question: What is the threshold on the bid/no-bid gate?
Have we agreed to cut the number of bids we submit?
What goes on the one-page discovery note?
